top.headline: Nasdaq 100 down about 2.7% as Nvidia earnings and Anthropic IPO loom; futures steady
top.why: The AI trade is at its most stretched point of the year going into Nvidia's first report without Jensen Huang, so after-the-bell results tonight can set the tone for Nasdaq futures tomorrow.
points: Monday close: S&P 500 -1.9%, Nasdaq 100 nearly -2.7%, Dow -1.4%; Nasdaq Composite -2.49% (Stocktwits, Eurasia Business News). Chip ETFs fell about 5%.
Nvidia fell 4.1% to $156.14, a third straight down session, after CNBC reported the board is not considering reinstating Huang; Kress is interim CEO.
Nvidia is expected to report revenue near $108.7bn (Fiscal.ai estimate) after the close today.
Tuesday morning futures were roughly flat (Dow +0.03%, S&P and Nasdaq-100 +0.1%) after the selloff (Stocktwits).
top.next: Nvidia Q3 results after the close Tue 17 Nov; Anthropic prices Wed 18 Nov and is expected to trade on Nasdaq as ANT on Thu 19 Nov.

top.headline: Anthropic IPO prices Wednesday: 825M shares at $70-78, demand reported 6x, trading Thursday as ANT
top.why: The first listing of a frontier lab is a read on appetite for AI valuations, landing in a Nasdaq correction and a day before Nvidia's results effect is priced in. Founders keep 50.1% of votes.
points: Terms: 825M shares at $70-78 (up to about $64.4B base); pricing expected Wed 18 Nov, Nasdaq trading Thu 19 Nov under ANT.
Valuation about $1T on outstanding shares, up to $1.4T fully diluted; Reuters-sourced demand figure of about 6x supply dates from last Thursday.
Separate $26B private placement from Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC Partners at the IPO price.

Reported Q3 revenue $16.96B (+47% q/q), run rate about $81B; filing discloses up to $120.5B of SpaceX compute commitments through 2029 (secondary report). Nasdaq fell 2.5% Monday into correction territory.
top.next: Pricing Wed 18 Nov; first trade Thu 19 Nov; Nvidia earnings after the bell Tue 17 Nov.

top.headline: GTA VI launch is 48 hours away: unlock times, no multiplayer, reviews unconfirmed
top.why: Launch-night planning: it unlocks at local midnight on 19 Nov, so New Zealand players start first and early impressions may appear from about 3 AM PT on 18 Nov.
points: Unlocks midnight local time on 19 Nov in each store region; Auckland midnight is 3 AM PT on 18 Nov (VICE).
Launches single-player only on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S; no online date announced.
Rockstar has not confirmed a review embargo; Bloomberg's Jason Schreier hosts a live Q&A 18 Nov, 8 AM PT.
Sensor Tower estimates nearly 15m pre-orders and about $1.5bn; it tops PlayStation Store charts in 46 countries (not Japan).
top.next: Early NZ unlock about 3 AM PT 18 Nov; Schreier Q&A 8 AM PT 18 Nov; global release 19 Nov.

stories.headline: Pochettino's United start nears: assistants sent ahead, Carrington on 18 Nov, Liverpool 22 Nov
stories.why: The managerial change is now in its handover phase; the first test is a Premier League trip to Liverpool four days after he starts work.
points: Appointed 13 Nov on a two-and-a-half-year deal after Michael Carrick's sacking; officially starts 18 Nov.
Yahoo and BBC report he has sent trusted assistants to Manchester ahead of his arrival and played down quick-turnaround concerns.
Still coaching USMNT until his final match this week; he urged Pep Guardiola to take the US job.
Reported (Yahoo, not confirmed by a core source): United made contact with a World Cup-winning manager before choosing him.
stories.next: Starts at Carrington 18 Nov; Liverpool away 22 Nov; Sporting Lisbon away 25 Nov.

stories.headline: December Fed hike is fully priced going into Wednesday's FOMC minutes
stories.why: With a hike priced, the minutes' count of October hike supporters is the main Fed read for rate-sensitive Nasdaq futures this week.
points: Fed held at 3.75-4.00% on 28 Oct after a September hike; Cook and Hammack dissented in favour of a 25bp rise (per Admirals, citing the Fed statement).
CME FedWatch showed a December hike fully priced at 05:12 GMT on 17 Nov (Admirals, citing Anadolu).
Minutes of the 27-28 Oct meeting expected Wed 18 Nov, 2:00 PM ET (11:00 AM PT); Admirals notes the Fed calendar had not yet posted the date.
Next rate decision is 9 Dec, with new projections.
stories.next: FOMC minutes Wed 18 Nov 11:00 AM PT (date unconfirmed on Fed calendar); FOMC decision 9 Dec.

stories.headline: Gulf tension widens: Bahrain reports Iranian air attacks, US reports a possible dirty-bomb plot
stories.why: Gulf shipping and security risk stays a live input for oil and index futures; the dirty-bomb item is an unverified report that Tehran denies.
points: Reuters (17 Nov): Bahrain says it intercepted Iranian air attacks; the IRGC says it targeted US radar.
Reuters (17 Nov): Trump says the US is taking seriously a report of a possible Iranian dirty-bomb plot in Washington; Tehran denies it.
AP (16 Nov): a third US aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East as Trump keeps options open in the Iran war.
stories.next: No dated catalyst found; watch Gulf headlines and oil into the US open (6:30 AM PT).

stories.headline: Chip-export curbs tighten: China data-centre limit advances, Nvidia forms export-control committee
stories.why: Policy risk is adding to the Nvidia leadership story and is part of why chips led Monday's drop.
points: Reuters exclusive (17 Nov): Trump's China data-centre curb advances despite Amazon, Google and Meta lobbying.
Reuters (17 Nov): Nvidia formed a board committee on national security and export controls.
AP (16 Nov): the administration moved to block China from indirect access to US AI technology.
stories.next: Nvidia commentary on export controls on tonight's call (17 Nov).

stories.headline: Ukraine hits Crimean bridge for a second day; Russia pounds Kyiv's bridges
stories.why: Escalation on both sides lands while the trilateral-meeting idea is still unsettled, so it cuts against near-term de-escalation hopes.
points: Reuters (17 Nov): Ukraine damaged the Crimean bridge in a major strike as Russia pounded bridges in Kyiv.
Russia says it was Ukraine's second day of strikes on the bridge and its biggest drone attack of the war (Russian claim, per Reuters).
Reuters (16 Nov): the IMF says it is near a $1.6bn deal with Ukraine once financing assurances are secured.
stories.next: No dated catalyst found; watch for any date for the three-power meeting and the IMF board decision.

stories.headline: Trump opens Asia trip in Manila with Quad talks, ahead of China visit and APEC
stories.why: Trade and security deals on this trip, and any Trump-Xi or Trump-Kim contact, can move tariff and chip-export expectations.
points: AP and Reuters (17 Nov): Trump arrived in the Philippines with economic deals and talks with allies; Quad talks in Manila come before his China visit.
Reuters: a Trump-Kim meeting on the APEC sidelines appears more likely, per analysts (analyst view, not confirmed).
Reuters: Shenzhen has banned horns and drones for Trump's visit and APEC.
stories.next: Quad talks in Manila, then China and APEC in Shenzhen this week (exact dates not in sources read).

stories.headline: Topstep bars new traders from 13 countries over coordinated fraud activity
stories.why: Topstep is on your watchlist and has moved from account-level bans to country-level restrictions, a tougher stance on ID bypass and hedging rings. Other firms are likely to watch this approach.
points: Topstep announced on X on 16 Nov that restrictions apply this week; it says fewer than 1,000 current traders are affected (Tokenpost counts 967 active).
Countries listed by Tokenpost: Andorra, Cambodia, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Macao, Mozambique, Namibia, Senegal, Serbia, Uzbekistan, Zimbabwe.
Topstep cited attempts to bypass ID verification and payment safeguards and coordinated trading across accounts that kept returning under new profiles.
Tokenpost reports existing affected traders have until the end of 2026 to offboard; I could not confirm this on a Topstep page.
stories.next: Topstep said it will share more detail on affected countries and next steps on its socials this week; check its help centre for the final list and offboarding terms.

stories.headline: Anthropic roadshow says Mythos ported Claude to AMD chips in about three days
stories.why: If it holds up, AI-written kernels weaken Nvidia's CUDA lock-in and strengthen Anthropic's hand with chipmakers. It is a roadshow claim with a narrow test.
points: Co-founder Tom Brown: Claude ran on AMD in about three days with almost no human intervention, versus 6-12 months for teams of dozens.
Slide footnote: test covered prompt processing on MI355X; reached a 'usable performance level' only.
AMD has a July deal for up to 2GW of MI450 chips with up to $5B investment into Anthropic; Nvidia is also in the $26B placement.
stories.next: Nvidia earnings tonight (17 Nov) and ANT debut Thu 19 Nov.

stories.headline: Meta pauses updated ad and commerce terms that would let it crawl merchant sites for AI training
stories.why: If you run Meta catalogue or ads, the paused terms would have made data access for AI a condition of service. The pause is not a withdrawal, so audit what Meta can take.
points: Changes to Commercial, Product Catalog, Self-Serve Ad and Ad Creative Generative AI terms were due 30 Oct 2026; Meta paused after backlash (NiemanLab/Reuters, via a secondary outlet).
Commentator advice: track what Meta sends you via UTMs, check server logs for Meta crawlers, and build owned channels (email, site).
Meta is reportedly testing a fee for Pages posting outside links.
stories.next: No date given for the terms to return; watch for a revised notice before BFCM.

stories.headline: Pope Leo rules out married priests for now, keeps Latin Mass limits
stories.why: His first public word on a long-debated reform: no change to priestly celibacy in the near term, with unity as the stated priority. It sets the tone of his papacy on two flashpoints for traditionalists and reformers alike.
points: Said on the flight back to Rome after a 12-day South America tour, reported Tuesday 17 Nov
Called married clergy 'a solution which in certain areas of the Church can cause division' but said 'it may be in the future that some things will change'
Will not reverse Francis's limits on the old Latin Mass, citing unity for the majority of Catholics
Francis also declined to act on a Vatican synod request to ordain married men in remote regions such as the Amazon
stories.next: No date set; Leo said he wants time for Catholics to weigh the Church's priorities.

stories.headline: Apologist Wes Huff faces plagiarism allegations over 2016 seminary paper
stories.why: A prominent popular apologist is under board review after scholars alleged uncredited borrowing; a test of integrity standards in public apologetics. Allegations so far, not findings.
points: Dan McClellan's 8 Nov video alleged Huff's 2016 Tyndale Seminary paper on John's Gospel copied large parts of Brian J. Wright's 2010 paper without citation
Stephen C. Carlson (Australian Catholic University) also alleged copying of his work
Huff said he takes the concerns 'seriously', is stepping back from public comment, and Apologetics Canada's board is reviewing
Wright told The Blaze he extends grace but that forgiveness does not remove accountability
stories.next: Outcome of the Apologetics Canada board review; no date given.

stories.headline: Megiddo dig finds Canaanite ritual pit with ram-shaped vessel, 5,000-year-old winepress
stories.why: Gives rare physical evidence of non-elite worship outside the temple at the site behind 'Armageddon', and early proof of winemaking in the region.
points: IAA salvage excavation along a highway beside Megiddo found a favissa from the end of the Late Bronze Age (c. 3,300 years ago)
Finds include a model shrine, Cypriot imports and an intact ram-shaped libation vessel
Rock-cut Early Bronze Age winepress (c. 5,000 years ago) described by directors Amir Golani and Barak Tzin as a 'smoking gun' for ancient wine
Interpretation that worshippers were kept outside the temple is the researchers' inference
stories.next: No date; full excavation publication pending.

stories.headline: Wegovy cuts BMI 13.5% in children aged 6 to 11, but vomiting common and BMI rebounds off drug
stories.why: First phase 3 data in under-12s with obesity: effective, but side effects and rebound suggest long-term treatment, and it is not approved for this age in the US.
points: STEP Young, NEJM 16 Nov: 167 children, 68 weeks; BMI -13.5% on semaglutide vs +2.7% on placebo (treatment-policy estimate; company's on-treatment figure -17.4%)
38.4% no longer classed as obese vs 2.1% on placebo
Vomiting 70% vs 29%; diarrhoea 62% vs 35%; nausea 58% vs 24%; serious adverse events 9% in both
BMI rose during a seven-week off-drug break; long off-drug data not yet available
stories.next: Regulatory filings for under-12s not reported; watch for any FDA/EMA submission.
stories.study: Phase 3 double-blind RCT, n=167, children 6-11 with obesity (mostly class II-III); industry-funded, modest size, limited off-treatment follow-up

stories.headline: Cochrane: kangaroo care probably cuts deaths and infections in small babies
stories.why: Strongest evidence yet for a free, low-tech intervention; the unanswered question is how many hours a day are needed.
points: Updated review of 49 RCTs, 7,724 low-birthweight or preterm newborns, more than doubling the 2016 review
Probably reduces in-hospital death, hospital-acquired infection and sepsis; may increase exclusive breastfeeding and reduce hypothermia
Effect clearest in low-resource settings
Insufficient evidence on whether longer than WHO's 8 hours a day helps more
stories.next: WHO guidance may be revisited; no date given.
stories.study: Cochrane systematic review of 49 RCTs, n=7,724 newborns; varied definitions of kangaroo care, most evidence from low- and middle-income countries

stories.headline: Cochrane: daily iron prevents anaemia in children, with little effect on common illnesses
stories.why: Reassures on a common worry that iron raises infection risk; useful context for supplementing children and adolescents.
points: Review of 114 studies, over 50,000 children and adolescents, led by Cornell
Iron alone probably reduces iron deficiency anaemia versus none or placebo
No effect on height or weight, or on cough, fever or respiratory illness
Many trials in Asia in under-fives; certainty for other combinations moderate to very low
stories.next: WHO guidelines (last updated 2016) may be reviewed; no date given.
stories.study: Cochrane systematic review, 114 studies, >50,000 children/adolescents; heterogeneous trials, mostly Asian under-5s

stories.headline: Blood p-tau217 plus age, sex and APOE gives 5- and 10-year cognitive decline risk estimate
stories.why: Moves Alzheimer's blood testing from positive/negative to a personalised risk figure, relevant as preventive therapies are studied.
points: Mayo Clinic, JAMA Neurology: 1,644 cognitively healthy people (Mayo Study of Aging), validated in 534 from ADNI, aged 60-90
Example: 75-year-old non-APOE e4 woman, 5-year MCI risk 5% at low p-tau217 vs 16% at high; 10-year 12% vs 35%
At high p-tau217, 5-year MCI risk ranged from 6% at 65 to 37% at 85
stories.next: Needs validation in more diverse groups before clinical use.
stories.study: Prospective cohort with external validation, n=2,178 total, ages 60-90; largely research cohorts, not tested in routine care

stories.headline: A Neanderthal-inherited gene variant shrinks visual brain areas and lowers schizophrenia risk
stories.why: A single inherited deletion with an unusually strong effect on brain anatomy, tracing to interbreeding, and a link to a disease risk. A neat window into what we carry from other humans.
points: PNAS study by Hugo Zeberg and Svante Pääbo (Max Planck, Leipzig), reported 16 Nov
Four-nucleotide deletion on chromosome 14 found in all five detailed Neanderthal genomes, absent in Denisovans, present only in people of non-African ancestry
Sits in a 59.7 kb chunk of DNA, too long to be from a shared ancestor, pointing to interbreeding
Carriers have reduced occipital (visual processing) lobe volume and lower schizophrenia risk
stories.next: Follow-up work on why reduced visual cortex relates to lower schizophrenia risk.
